title.en: Finite-mode survival distinguishability at horizon card minus one

statement.en: On nonempty finite state spaces and real matrix families Mode -> S -> S -> ℝ (survival probabilities when nonnegative substochastic), two states agree on all mode words iff they agree through length card - 1; sharp at card - 1, switch-sensitive, and separates C2 states.

laws.en: Via Krylov subspace stabilization over (S -> ℝ) for arbitrary real matrices Mode -> S -> S -> ℝ (interpreted as survival probabilities when nonnegative substochastic), two states agree on all mode words iff they agree through length Fintype.card S - 1 (survival_indistinguishable_iff_le_card_pred).

For every positive n, the one-mode countdown matrix on Fin (n + 1) makes states 0 and 1 agree on every word shorter than n while separating them at exact length n = Fintype.card (Fin (n + 1)) - 1 (countdown_attains_card_pred).

On a three-state two-mode operator, constant sequences [false]*k and [true]*k keep states 0 and 1 equal to 1 for every length k, whereas the two-step switch [false, true] separates 1 from 0 (three_state_mode_switch_counterexample).

Restricting Becoming.OplaxHistory.C2CoupledAlignmentWitness to live configurations (Bool x Bool) x Bool yields a finite sub-stochastic operator separating same-projection states finInPhase and finAntiPhase at length 1 <= card - 1 (c2_coupled_survival_separation).

Abbreviating stepOp to FiniteKrylov.stepLinearMap while keeping local defs survVec and krylovSub bridged via survVec_eq_finiteKrylov and krylovSub_eq_finiteKrylov, exact FiberLumpable compresses survival indistinguishability to length <= card O - 1 (survival_indistinguishable_iff_le_obs_pred; substochastic, since Markov kernels give survVec = 1).

hypotheses.en: Lean v4.30.0-rc2 + Mathlib standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) in Mathlib periphery; assumes finite nonempty state space [Fintype S] [Nonempty S] and arbitrary real matrices K : Mode -> S -> S -> ℝ against the all-ones vector (interpreted as survival probabilities when rows are nonnegative substochastic).

does_not_show.en: Does not prove finite-horizon distinguishability bounds for infinite-state, continuous-state, or non-stationary transition kernels.

Under normalized stochastic Markov rows, survVec K w s = 1 for all words w, so FiberLumpable observable-horizon compression carries non-trivial distinguishing content only for substochastic/real survival matrices.
Agreement across arbitrary single-mode constant sequences does not ensure indistinguishability under mode switches.
Exact finite-matrix separation on frozen greedy policies never establishes by itself that online learning agents keep stationary or time-homogeneous transition kernels.

detail.en: countdown_attains_card_pred proves tightness of Fintype.card S - 1 for every n >= 1; three_state_mode_switch_counterexample shows all constant-mode words fail to separate states 0 and 1 while [false, true] separates them.
